runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q1; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order at the operator's word ("Yes start with those"), interactive dispatch under the canonical brief, five analysts in parallel (NRG, OGE, PAM, PCG, PNW), lock held by the main session; the brief's one departure is the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25. Price **$79.50 an ADS** ($3.18 a share; 2026-10-23, aggregator, flagged) x **1,340.1M shares** (53.60M ADS; the cover tool's 1,359.6M less 19.9M cancelled in April 2026 and 3.5M held for the employee plan) = cap **$4,261.5M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year, 2026-10-23; the functional currency is the US dollar). Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE), read by parts: power generation decides at 59.6% of five-year operating profit (oil and gas 24.2%, the TGS and Transener holding 10.2%, petrochemicals 6.0%); its price is written by the Secretariat of Energy and paid by CAMMESA, a state agency, and over the window moved from dollars to pesos with indexation to pesos without it, through about twenty resolutions, to a marginal-price market only in November 2025 (Res. 400/25); CAMMESA paid December 2023 and January 2024 in sovereign bonds; the 20-F (`0001292814-26-002185`) says the reforms' "full impact ... remains uncertain"; no unread filing can say what future governments will pay generators. Evidence for the business recorded: generation's dollar operating income held at $204M to $375M a year through 2020 to 2025; S&P upgrade to B. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash before interest, investee profit counted only as dividends received, maintenance case $371M a year (466 to 406, -3.4% a year), all spending $88M; range **$40.55 to $105.11 an ADS all-equity (central)**, equity-only $2.99 to $67.55; fair price **$23.69 an ADS all-equity** ($0.95 a share; equity-only $15.17); the price inside the range, no case earns the floor (best 6.6% on enterprise value); about $1.4B of growth spending in the window bought no growth in owner cash. Facts after the stop: receivables $948M at June 2026; cash tax $23M against $574M charged over 2021 to 2025, the 2024 tax in a $226M payment plan; about $7B of committed projects (Rincon de Aranda shale oil $4.52B, a urea plant $2.7B); net debt from $411M (2024) to $1,319M; purchases from SACDE, a related party, $65M to $103M to $223M (2023 to 2025); senior management paid 3.6% of the annual market-value gain, capped; buybacks at about $20 to $23 an ADS (2019, 2022) and $58.65 to $59.50 (2025) under a stated $60 cap. Competitors (operating income on total assets, XBRL, flagged): PAM 9.1%, YPF about 2.5%, VIST about 12%, TGS 8% to 31%; non-SEC rivals not read. Tooling: `tools/run.py` printed nothing usable for this IFRS filer; `Screens/cover_shares.py` count out of date. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; three pathspec commits, own paths only; 35 citations clean (the analyst's check). Contamination declared: file names in listings and the map, one commit subject; none opened. Position note filled at the fold: not held. No alert (closed before Q7).
runs.narr: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q1: the deciding part, power generation, earns a price the Argentine state writes, has rewritten about twenty times since 2019, and once paid in bonds. Computation only: range $40.55 to $105.11 an ADS all-equity vs $79.50, fair $23.69; the price sits inside the range but no case earns the floor. A $7B build-out (shale oil and a urea plant) has begun with net debt tripling.
